narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>B minus eigh can be negative. I am sure eigh minus b, all squared, is bigger.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it with eigh as seven and b as two. Five squared is twenty five, and minus five squared is also twenty five.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The two squares came out the same, so his claim fails.
removed_beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows (a − b)² > (b − a)²; a = 7, b = 2 gives 5² = 25 and (−5)² = 25; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>To check, try any pair of numbers, such as eigh as three and b as eight.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Minus five squared and five squared both give twenty five, so the squares agree.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the answer card; check line a = 3, b = 8: (3 − 8)² = 25 and (8 − 3)² = 25

old_misconception.wrong_answer: eigh minus b, all squared, is bigger
old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says (a − b)² is bigger because a − b comes first and b − a is negative. Both expand to a² − 2ab + b², so they are equal.
